title: Stable usage linter newline handling
body:
# Issue
-   #183049.

# Summary
From the issue, the current stable usage linter approach doesn't correctly handle situations where statements are spread over multiple lines because it parses line by line, this can happen when clang-format splits the line, like with;
```cpp
AOTI_TORCH_EXPORT AOTITorchError
this_is_a_very_long_function(StableIValue** ret_value);
```

This function won't get picked up and inserted into `shim_function_versions.txt` for tracking, this was spotted [here](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/179421#discussion_r3037232042) in one of my other PRs, where we worked around it with a `clang-format off` comment. In this PR it was discovered that there's 12 C shims that fell through the cracks, like [this one here](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/9b859de038ee65c6d44939a894453856e24d632f/torch/csrc/stable/c/shim.h#L64-L65), where the formatter broke in the same place as the problematic example.

Before this PR the PreprocessorTracker returned whether a line was a comment or whether it should be parsed using a single-line regex for relevant function names.

This PR introduces an accumulation helper that collects the text between a start and an end pattern and then calls a handler on it. This also means that to be able to find the relevant patterns, we need to provide it patterns to look for, and their handler callbacks.

Code has gotten pretty dense... more so than I would've liked, especially `MatcherAccumulator`. I introduced a new unit test `tools/test/test_stable_shim_utils.py` to test it specifically. New logic is hooked into the usage_linter and version_linter, which does makes those files a bit simpler.

In the linked issue I mentioned `clang-query`, I do think that is worth giving another look next time anything around these linters comes up. It may require some extra tooling to make that work in CI and run it with the various preprocessor define flags, but it would completely do away with the string-based parsing of C++ that's happening now, which is really hard to get right.

For now, this keeps things moving forward.

 @janeyx99
